speaker: Doctor
text: Let me start by asking: When did you first notice the rash, and has it spread or changed in appearance since then?

speaker: Patient
text: 47-year-old male. The patient presents with a rash that started last night, finding it very concerning. He does not recall being exposed to any new environmental stimuli such as detergents or plants like poison ivy. He mentions he recently started seeing a primary care provider for arthritis management and a new onset cough.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is concerning; can you describe the appearance of the rash and tell me if the cough is dry or productive? Also, have you noticed any joint swelling or morning stiffness related to your arthritis?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Rash on the upper half of the back. I also have Concern over sudden onset, Recent cough, Unaware of exposure to new environmental stimuli, Mucositis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Drug-induced Lupus Erythematosus (likely secondary to new medication for arthritis).

REQUEST TEST: Anti-histone antibodies, ANA panel, and ESR.
REQUEST IMAGES: Full body skin map showing upper back rash distribution.
